Blinds $50 / $100. Action moves clockwise; preflop starts left of the big blind, later streets left of the dealer button.
Ties are broken by kickers — the highest unpaired cards. Suits never break ties; equal hands split the pot.
An ace plays high or low in a straight (A-2-3-4-5 is the lowest straight). All-ins create side pots you can only win up to your stake.

With three cards a straight is rarer than a flush, so it ranks higher. A-2-3 counts as the lowest straight.
Dealer needs Queen high or better to qualify. Beat a qualifying dealer: Ante and Play pay 1:1. Dealer doesn't qualify: Ante pays 1:1, Play pushes.
Pair Plus pays on your hand alone, whatever the dealer holds. Ante bonus pays whenever you play, win or lose. Optimal play: Play with Q-6-4 or better.

European single-zero wheel: 37 pockets (0–36). Pick a chip value, tap the board to place it, then spin. Bets stay on the board between spins.
When the ball lands on 0, every outside bet (red/black, odd/even, dozens, columns, 1–18/19–36) loses. Only a straight bet on 0 wins.
Every bet carries the same 2.70% house edge — no betting system changes that.
